title: Slovakia Weighs Tax Reversal as Households Endure Stubborn Inflation · 28 Aug
keywords: Slovakia, transaction tax, inflation, fiscal policy, cost of living, eurozone, National Bank of Slovakia, Eurostat, SME, competitiveness, EU fiscal rules, household spending, central Europe
notes: The Slovak government is signalling it may scrap its controversial transaction tax next year, reversing a measure that drew sharp criticism from the business community. The move comes as the country grapples with inflation that, while easing from earlier peaks, remains above the euro-area average and continues to squeeze household budgets. Together, the two developments present a defining test of the government's economic credibility heading into the next political cycle.
